batch_node.name: Samsite users seed v0.2.0
batch_node.description: Seeds the people in the samsite story as identity_core `human` nodes: george (the operator reproducing and modeling the system in TAP) and Sam (Sam Aydlette, author of the original samaydlette.com system). A human is found again by its `handle` (identity_core's natural key), so each carries one. Each carries the dimension samsite.story = actor, which this batch also seeds as a dimension node. The landing search scopes its MATCH (u:identity_core__human) to that dimension, so another plugin's humans on the same grid do not appear on the samsite landing. Edges/roles and projection placement are intentionally not seeded here. v0.2.0: moved from computing_core `user` to identity_core `human` (samsite-tap#33): computing_core retired `user`, whose meaning duplicated `human` (computing-core-tap#27). The nodes have fresh entity ids because a row cannot change type. On a grid seeded from v0.1.0, the old `user` rows stay until computing_core's 0.5 migration deletes them, and the landing no longer matches them. The v0.1.0 'Readers' node is dropped: it was an audience, not a person. `human` has no description field, so the per-person notes live here: george reproduces and models the samsite system in TAP; Sam Aydlette wrote the original samaydlette.com system and its FedRAMP 20x compliance machinery.

node.name: samsite.story
node.description: Marks the entities that belong to the samsite story itself, as opposed to anything else that happens to share the grid. Value `actor` marks the people samsite seeds (george, Sam), so that the samsite landing search matches only those identity_core__human nodes and not every human on the grid. The AWS side is scoped by its tags.Project = samsite; a human has no tags field, so this dimension does that job for the people.
